title: Know which requests never left

blocks.text: An online bookshop sends its purchases to the acquirer through `Submitter.submit`, in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/Submitter.java`. Yesterday a merchant whose name and location ran one character too long in field 43 took the link down. The purchase in flight beside it was approved by the host but reported to the shop as unanswered, and the support team couldn't tell which of the two had actually reached the host.

Finish the three places marked `TODO` so that every `Result` tells the truth: `ANSWERED` with the host's response, `NO_ANSWER` for a request that went out and heard nothing back, and `NOT_SENT` with a reason for a request that never left. The `packager` passed to the constructor is the one the link's channel uses. About 10 lines in total.
The tests run a real QMUX against a test host on the far side of its queues, and some of them use a network whose fields are not the standard's lengths.

cases.says: a request the link can carry is sent once and the caller gets the host's answer
a request that cannot be packed is reported as not sent and is never queued for the host
a request that went out and got no answer is reported as unanswered, not as unsent
the check catches any field that does not fit, not only the one that failed before
whether a request fits is decided by the packager of the link it goes to, not by the standard's

origin.section: 2.2 A Message That Doesn't Pack Fails on the Channel Thread

concepts: A message that does not pack fails on the channel thread: the caller sees only a timeout and the 2.1.7 adaptor drops the link, so pack with the link's packager before queueing and report such a message as not sent.
